html:
The Tonkawa are a Native American people of central Texas, now based in Oklahoma. Their language, no longer spoken, was an isolate, related to no other known language.

They lived as hunters and gatherers on the prairies of central Texas, following bison and deer, and became mounted hunters once horses spread north from New Spain. They were often at war with the Apache and later the Comanche. In the 1740s and 1750s the Spanish built missions on the San Xavier River for them and their neighbours, but these did not last.

In the 1800s the Tonkawa often served as scouts for Texans and the army against the Comanche, which made them enemies of many tribes. In 1862, during the American Civil War, a force of other tribes attacked them in Indian Territory and killed many, in what is called the Tonkawa massacre. The survivors were settled in Oklahoma in 1884. The Tonkawa Tribe of Indians of Oklahoma now has more than 700 citizens. Their neighbours on the coast were the Karankawa; to the north lived the Wichita.
